statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete: all 58 catalog checks have conclusive outcomes.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with legacy jQuery and advertising stack
page.notes: Representative coverage: homepage, editorial article, game detail, game search, login and a 404 state. Excluded authenticated account internals, signup completion, ad click-throughs and destructive/commercial transactions because they require credentials or external commitments.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot remains the same light page and the stylesheet probe found no prefers-color-scheme handling.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() returned no active animations, so no non-essential motion persisted.

checkOutcomes.method: Contrast emulation probe plus Lighthouse accessibility audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: No prefers-contrast/forced-colors CSS was found, and Lighthouse found 248 insufficient-contrast nodes.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature probe and route observation
checkOutcomes.evidence: No view-transition CSS or API usage was present; navigation between the sampled MPA routes is an abrupt full-document swap.
No scroll-linked animation surface or scroll-driven animation was observed, so the page does not use a main-thread scroll animation anti-pattern.
The sampled core controls use ordinary links, buttons and scrolling; no custom gesture interaction that fights platform behavior was observed.
The long home and article templates have static chrome and no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or position-aware header behavior.
No tooltip/menu requiring anchor positioning was found on sampled core paths; the consent surface is viewport-modal rather than anchored UI.
The article and detail pages expose breadcrumbs, ordered headings, and clear related-content navigation that preserve orientation.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load screenshots at desktop and mobile
checkOutcomes.evidence: A consent interstitial blocks all content on every fresh page load before interaction.
The blocking consent surface is a custom div with role=dialog rather than a native dialog; rejection requires opening Manage options.
Ads, fixed-width sidebars, dense navigation, rankings and banners dominate the viewport and visually compete with editorial content.
The page declares viewport width=1580; Chrome renders a 1440 CSS-pixel layout scaled to 25%, with 140px horizontal overflow and unreadably tiny content.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature probe and multi-template viewport metadata
checkOutcomes.evidence: No @container/container-type usage was found and sampled templates hard-code viewport widths of 1000 or 1580 instead of adapting components.
The first focusable link computed outline-style none and zero width; many visible header links are only 16–24px high, below comfortable touch size.
The home, article, game detail, search and login pages have descriptive Japanese titles/headings and recognizable navigation to core content.
Game discovery links lead to detail/article pages and the login path provides email/password plus social sign-in controls; no auth wall blocks public content.
The login fields are not required and expose no aria-invalid or browser validation message on blank submission, weakening actionable recovery.
Lighthouse mobile reports LCP 5.7s, TBT 420ms, Speed Index 12.1s and TTI 20.1s; the independent trace reports LCP 4.15s.
Observed CLS was 0.0001 in the layout capture and 0.042 in Lighthouse, both in the good range.
Lighthouse reports 4.9s main-thread work, 1.6s JavaScript execution and 420ms TBT; the trace recorded long tasks.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary and Lighthouse delivery insights
checkOutcomes.evidence: The load transferred 3.62MB over 192 requests; parser-inserted jQuery/ad/basic scripts and CSS are render-blocking candidates, with 2.56s estimated render-blocking savings.
Lighthouse estimates 660KiB unused JavaScript and 44KiB unused CSS, while ad/analytics bundles dominate script transfer.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility and login DOM probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The header information image lacks alt text, and the email/password controls have no associated labels or ARIA labels.
Lighthouse found 248 contrast failures, including 12px #929292 text on white at 3.11:1.
The consent manager injects several additional H1 elements and the focused logo link has no visible outline or box shadow.
The forced desktop canvas is scaled to 25% on a 360px device, making navigation and article text too small to read comfortably.
Fixed width viewport metadata prevents normal mobile reflow, and numerous navigation targets are only 16–30px high.
Lighthouse captured SyntaxError: Identifier tabSelector has already been declared on the home page.
Although doctype/charset are valid, 99 of 100 images lack explicit dimensions, 99 use legacy formats, and Lighthouse reports an unsized image.
Lighthouse reports a deprecated API warning, third-party-cookie issues and a DevTools inspector issue.
Home, article, game detail, search and login pages expose descriptive titles; public content pages include meta descriptions.
Lighthouse found 19 non-crawlable anchors and the viewport meta uses fixed widths rather than device-width.

checkOutcomes.method: Canonical, robots, sitemap, status and discoverability probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Public pages return 200, expose canonical URLs, robots.txt and sitemap.xml are reachable, and no accidental noindex signal was observed.
The article provides NewsArticle and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD plus complete Open Graph title, URL, image and description matching visible content.
HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP only declares frame-ancestors; 12 cookies lack Secure and many use SameSite=None.

checkOutcomes.method: Tracker and HAR analysis before consent
checkOutcomes.evidence: A fresh load contacted 34 third-party origins and 8 known tracker domains; 190 of 192 HAR requests were classified cross-origin and 3.47MB was transferred cross-origin.
The sampled login supports password and social providers but exposes no site passkey/WebAuthn flow; no permission prompt fired on load.
X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent; HSTS max-age is only one day, and cookie posture is weak.
Raw server HTML is 2.25MB, is not a JS shell, retains title/H1/description, and contains 81% of rendered content tokens.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative route, overlay and error-state exercise
checkOutcomes.evidence: Sampled MPA routes loaded usable server-rendered content, the consent manager remained in viewport, and no blank runtime shell occurred.
GameWith is a public editorial/content website rather than an installed app; no manifest/offline app promise is needed for its primary reading task.
checkOutcomes.reason: GameWith is a public editorial/content website rather than an installed app; no manifest/offline app promise is needed for its primary reading task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: An invalid representative URL returns an intentional HTTP 404 response rather than a misleading 200 shell.
The audited site is deliberately Japanese-language and Japan-market focused; no locale switcher, multi-currency, cross-zone scheduling, or international audience promise was observed.

checkOutcomes.reason: The audited site is deliberately Japanese-language and Japan-market focused; no locale switcher, multi-currency, cross-zone scheduling, or international audience promise was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Consent screenshot, DOM and pre-consent tracker capture
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent wall offers a one-click Consent action but no equivalent one-click Reject action, while a fresh load already contacts extensive ad/tracker infrastructure.
Email/password inputs are not required and blank submission produced no browser validation message or aria-invalid state.
Email and password fields omit autocomplete=username/current-password tokens and lack explicit labels.
The account flow relies on passwords/social providers and presents no passkey option; form controls also lack modern autofill tokens.

checkOutcomes.method: Images primitive and Lighthouse image-delivery insight
checkOutcomes.evidence: 99/100 images are legacy formats, 24 lack srcset, 9 are oversized, and Lighthouse estimates 733KiB image-delivery savings.
The page performs 192 requests, ships 660KiB estimated-unused JavaScript and executes large advertising/analytics bundles before a core task.
Third-party/cross-origin delivery accounts for 190 requests and 3.47MB, including ad-tech, analytics and consent infrastructure disproportionate to a text-heavy homepage.
The site is content-rich and agent-relevant, but exposes no WebMCP/agentic tool interface for search or game discovery; agents must scrape links/forms.
No user task observed in the sampled pages requires on-device generation or summarisation; omitting built-in AI is not a quality failure here.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user task observed in the sampled pages requires on-device generation or summarisation; omitting built-in AI is not a quality failure here.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/post heap snapshots around 10 consent manage/back cycles
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 cycles self size rose about 0.90MB (1.2%) and closures rose by only 3; this single comparison does not show unbounded retained growth.
A text-heavy homepage retains about 76.7MB self size across 1.29M heap nodes, a large footprint consistent with extensive ad/analytics machinery.
No Detached* constructor appears among the top retained constructors, closures remained effectively flat (34,836 to 34,839), and the repeated cycle did not show listener-like growth.

principleOutcomes.reason: The audited site is deliberately Japanese-language and Japan-market focused; no locale switcher, multi-currency, cross-zone scheduling, or international audience promise was observed.

paths.description: Homepage and primary game-discovery entry; global layout, consent, navigation, performance, privacy and asset template.
Representative editorial NewsArticle template and long-form reading journey.
Representative game entity/detail template with review and related-content surfaces.
Primary game-finding surface and agent-relevant search journey.
Primary authentication form for labels, validation, autofill and modern-auth review.
Representative unknown route for HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: No system-driven dark theme
findings.evidence: Dark emulation leaves the interface light and CSS contains no color-scheme handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surfaces/text through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Contrast preferences and baseline contrast are not supported
findings.evidence: No contrast preference CSS was found; Lighthouse identified 248 contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text/UI contrast to WCAG minimums and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: No View Transition usage was found across sampled route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-position feedback
findings.evidence: Long editorial pages use static chrome with no progress or scroll-state response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header using declarative CSS where supported.

findings.summary: Consent interstitial blocks every fresh visit
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show all page content dimmed and blocked before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent notice where lawful and provide equally prominent accept/reject actions.

findings.summary: Consent UI is a custom dialog implementation
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows a role=dialog div rather than the native dialog primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for truly modal consent, with correct focus restoration, Escape behavior and explicit actions.

findings.summary: Advertising and dense chrome crowd out content
findings.evidence: The first viewport is dominated by ad creative, multiple nav rows, sidebars and rankings.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce first-viewport ad/chrome density and prioritize one clear editorial content column.

findings.summary: Mobile receives a scaled desktop canvas
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the page uses a 1440px CSS viewport at 0.25 scale, fixed width=1580 and 140px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Set viewport width=device-width, remove fixed 1000/1580 canvases, and rebuild templates with fluid intrinsic layout.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to available space
findings.evidence: No container query features were found and templates hard-code desktop viewport widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and adapt grids/cards with @container plus intrinsic sizing.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch target support are weak
findings.evidence: Focused links have no visible outline; many header links are only 16–24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strong :focus-visible styling and make interactive hit areas at least 44 CSS px where practical.

findings.summary: Login errors are not surfaced early or accessibly
findings.evidence: Blank login controls remain valid with no validation message or aria-invalid state.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark required fields, validate after interaction, and announce actionable errors in a live region.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses user-centric targets
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 5.7s LCP, 420ms TBT, 12.1s Speed Index and 20.1s TTI.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP/interaction work, prioritize the hero/content, and defer non-critical advertising and analytics.

findings.summary: Main-thread work is excessive
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 4.9s main-thread work and 1.6s JS execution, with long tasks corroborated by trace/layout captures.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary scripts, schedule non-critical work, and split long tasks below 50ms.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is heavy and blocking
findings.evidence: 192 requests transfer 3.62MB; parser-inserted jQuery, ad and basic scripts sit on the critical path.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, modernize dependencies, preload only LCP-critical assets and set durable caches.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused code ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 660KiB unused JS and 44KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route/component, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and conditionally load ad/search features.

findings.summary: Some content and login controls lack accessible names
findings.evidence: The information image lacks alt; login email/password fields have no labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use alt="" for decorative images and visible label elements for every authentication field.

findings.summary: Widespread text contrast failures
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 248 failures, including 3.11:1 small gray text on white.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust color tokens to meet WCAG AA in every normal, hover, focus and disabled state.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and heading structure are disrupted
findings.evidence: The consent UI adds multiple H1s and focused navigation has no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page H1, use dialog headings below it semantically, and implement visible :focus-visible states.

findings.summary: A production JavaScript syntax error is logged
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured duplicate declaration of tabSelector.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the duplicate declaration and add console-error monitoring to release checks.

findings.summary: Images lack robust sizing and modern delivery
findings.evidence: 99/100 images lack dimensions and 99 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height, srcset/sizes, lazy loading and AVIF/WebP variants from the image pipeline.

findings.summary: Deprecated and inspector issues remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated API warning and a DevTools inspector issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and clear DevTools Issues before deployment.

findings.summary: Interactive tabs use non-crawlable JavaScript URLs
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 19 non-crawlable anchors; DOM probes show javascript:void(0) href values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for local state changes and real href URLs for navigable destinations.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP protections are weak
findings.evidence: CSP only restricts framing; 12 cookies lack Secure and many use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and set Secure, HttpOnly where appropriate, and Lax/Strict SameSite defaults.

findings.summary: Tracking begins with an extensive third-party footprint
findings.evidence: A fresh load reaches 34 third-party origins and 8 known trackers before consent interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential tags until consent, remove redundant vendors, and batch/minimize analytics.

findings.summary: Login offers no phishing-resistant passkey option
findings.evidence: The account UI exposes password/social login but no site passkey flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add WebAuthn/passkey registration and authentication as a first-class sign-in option.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent; HSTS is one day.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, strict referrer/permissions policies and lengthen HSTS after deployment verification.

findings.summary: Consent choices are asymmetrical
findings.evidence: Consent is one click, while rejection is hidden behind Manage options despite processing by up to 300 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject all with equal prominence and keep granular management secondary.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autofill semantics
findings.evidence: Email/password controls have empty autocomplete values and no explicit labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete=username and current-password and pair each control with a label.

findings.summary: The image pipeline wastes bytes
findings.evidence: 99 legacy images, 24 missing srcset and 9 oversized images were detected; Lighthouse estimates 733KiB savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate appropriately sized AVIF/WebP variants and responsive source sets.

findings.summary: Background and unused work is excessive
findings.evidence: The initial page performs 192 requests and ships an estimated 660KiB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics/ads after consent and idle or interaction, and remove unused execution paths.

findings.summary: Third-party cost is disproportionate to content value
findings.evidence: Cross-origin delivery accounts for 190 requests and 3.47MB on a mostly editorial page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove duplicate tags and defer optional vendors.

findings.summary: Game search is not exposed as a structured agent capability
findings.evidence: Agents can read server HTML but must scrape navigation/search affordances.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider a narrowly scoped read-only WebMCP search tool with clear parameters and safe output.

findings.summary: Homepage memory footprint is large
findings.evidence: Heap summary retains 76.7MB self size and 1.29M nodes before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad/analytics libraries, DOM volume and long-lived caches; set a memory budget and re-measure.

taskList.title: Rebuild templates for true mobile reflow and accessible targets
Gate and reduce advertising/analytics third parties
Fix contrast, labels, focus and heading semantics
Make consent symmetric, compact and semantic
Harden CSP, cookies and browser policies
Repair crawlable anchors and production console errors
Modernize login validation, autofill and passkeys
Add system theme and progressive navigation polish
Evaluate a safe agent-readable game search capability
